messages:
alex: Customer report — streaming SSE session drops mid-response and then reconnects; they see partial output and later get a 429 mid-stream which their client treats as terminal. Billing shows doubled token counts. urgent please :alarm_clock:

maya: TL;DR — 429 returned mid-stream, client reconnects and resumes, duplicated token accounting. Customer provided small repro and some headers.

sam: hey — i'm the customer dev. repro steps below. it happens reliably against our prod key. stream stops with a 429 event after ~40s, client reopens connection and we get the rest. billing dashboard then shows both sessions billed.

sam: repro (curl):
```
curl -N "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=redwood-large" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-xxx" \
  -H "X-Client-Id: acme-frontend" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: frontend-req-9876" \
  --data-raw '{"prompt":"long streaming reply","max_tokens":4000}'
```

sam: sample SSE they see (trimmed):
```
event: data
data: {"delta":"first chunk...\n"}

# later
event: error
data: {"status":429,"code":"quota_exceeded","retry_after":15}

# client reconnects and gets continuation chunks
event: data
data: {"delta":"continued...final\n"}
```

maya: customer says billing shows ~4500 tokens used twice (start+reconnect). they suspect token-ledger not being reconciled when mid-stream 429 happens.

support-bot: @maya opened ticket INC-2026-246 with priority P1 and attached initial logs.

maya: steps i tried with them: 1) confirmed they use long-poll SSE (no chunk buffering) 2) asked for full request/response headers (they sent x-request-id: rq-21a9, x-region: us-west2) 3) verified they don't set Last-Event-ID.

diego: assigning to eng-sre to check rate limiter behavior for streaming connections. my immediate hypothesis: rate-limiter treats the reconnect as a new session and the earlier partial session's token accounting wasn't rolled back. also possible upstream proxy returned 429 due to burst throttle.

nate: reassigning to eng-runtime. two things to check server-side: whether we emit a final "event: session_end" with a session id when we cut with 429, and whether billing ledger records are tied to session_id vs connection_id. if ledger uses ephemeral conn id we could double-bill on reconnect.

nate: asking for the following from SRE/customer: tcpdump/pcap of the TLS session (if allowed), full response headers around the 429 (we need x-rate-limit-* headers), full x-request-id and the server x-internal-request-id we generate (if they have it).

sam: i attached the raw response headers for the 429:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 12:34:56 GMT
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
X-Request-Id: rq-21a9
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 161
X-RateLimit-Retry-After: 15
X-Internal-Request-Id: int-7f2b
X-Usage-Tokens-Emitted: 2345
```

maya: thats perfect — we have X-Usage-Tokens-Emitted on the 429. need to see if a subsequent session logs the same original session id or a new one. if new, that's probably why billing counted both.

ingrid: billing note — when we see duplicated token reports with different session ids we currently attribute both to customer. we can do a manual reconciliation if engineering confirms duplication. please open a billing adjustment request with reference to rq-21a9 once eng confirms root cause.

diego: infra checks to run (SRE):
- locate ingress logs for int-7f2b and rq-21a9
- check rate-limiter instance that returned 429 (node id + container)
- verify if we emitted a session_end/event with session_id on 429 path
- check ledger service for entries: session_id -> tokens_emitted and whether session state moved to "finalized" or remained "inflight"

nate: runtime checklist (eng-runtime):
- confirm how token accounting happens for streaming: do we persist per-session counters immediately or only on session close?
- if only on close, mid-stream 429 may have persisted partial counts but not reconciliation on reconnect. need to inspect commit path in billing adapter.

maya: quick mitigation suggestions for customer:
- client can set Idempotency-Key per top-level request (they tried but said reconnect still treated as new)
- we can patch gateway to look for Last-Event-ID header from client and map to original session if present
- short-term: ask engineering for a rollback/credit if duplication confirmed (billing already flagged it)

sam: happy to add Last-Event-ID support if you expose it; we can also avoid auto-reconnect in frontend for now.

diego: SRE to collect logs and paste key snippets here. i pulled ingress logs and found the 429 came from rate-limiter pod rate-limiter-3. snippet: 
```
[ingress] int-7f2b rq-21a9 accepted tokens=2345 conn_id=c-5b2 partial=true action=throttle reason=burst
[rate-limiter-3] rq-21a9 returned 429 remaining=0 reset=161 retry_after=15
```

diego: ledger snapshot (redacted): 
```
session_id: s-3a1 (conn_id=c-5b2) tokens_emitted:2345 state: inflight
# reconnect created session s-3a2 (conn_id=c-6d7) tokens_emitted:2200 state: finalized
```

nate: that seems to confirm: the first session remained inflight so when reconnect billed the second, both were counted. runtime stored partial tokens_emitted on the first but didn't finalize/roll back on 429. we need a fix: either finalize + mark as errored (and bill partial) or roll back partial and not bill until finalization.

ingrid: from billing POV, customers should not be double-charged. please indicate desired behavior: either bill only fully-finalized sessions, or bill incremental but ensure duplicates are deduped by session_id associated with Idempotency-Key.

diego: action items:
- SRE: collect full logs and add to incident INC-2026-246 (done)
- eng-runtime (nate): implement short-term patch to mark inflight sessions that received a 429 as "errored-finalized" so ledger doesn't double-bill on reconnect. roll-forward fix to be tested on staging.
- eng-billing (ingrid): prepare a manual credit flow for affected accounts; hold any automated billing deductions for these request ids until reconciliation.
- support (maya): ask customer for network capture if available and confirm they will disable auto-reconnect client-side until we deploy fix.

nate: I'll push a canary to staging with a change to stamp 429-terminated sessions as finalized-errored and expose telemetry. estimate 2d to deploy and QA.

maya: thanks all. sam — we will prioritize this. i'll keep you updated and file the billing adjustment once nate confirms the behavior. sorry about the disruption :applause:

sam: appreciate it. i left the full HAR in the ticket and flagged the account id acme-42. let me know if you need anything else.

support-bot: Incident INC-2026-246 updated: status -> investigating.

nate: FYI for timeline: if we patch staging well, we can do a canary to us-west2 tomorrow and monitor X-Usage-Tokens-Emitted trends for duplication.

alex: closing loop: be sure to add a note to docs about recommended client behavior on SSE 429s (avoid automatic reconnect without Last-Event-ID or persistent stream id).

maya: will add to support FAQ once we have final guidance.
